'''Frederick Purser''' (1839–30 January 1910) was an Irish mathematician, author, and member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]].  He was a younger brother to mathematician [[John Purser (mathematician)|John Purser]].<ref>[http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/history/Biographies/Purser.html John Purser] at the [[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]</ref>

==Life and career==
Born in Dublin, Frederick attended a boarding school run by his uncle Richard Biggs in [[Wiltshire, England]], then attended [[Trinity College Dublin]] (TCD), where he was Scholar (1859), and got BA (1860) and MA (1864). He was elected a Fellow there in 1879. He was appointed [[Trinity College Dublin Chair of Natural Philosophy|Professor of Natural Philosophy]] in 1902 and served in the role until his death.  He contributed articles to the 1911 [[Encyclopedia Britannica]].<ref>[https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Author:Frederick_Purser Author:Frederick Purser] Wikisource</ref>
